approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a score-ranked population and fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process using only that session's accepted observations. For each purchase it follows one coherent sampled function through eight bounded mutation waves, choosing mutation sources uniformly from the four visited graphs with highest sampled values. It then buys distinct cached path maxima; after three non-improving batches, an independently applied final screen permits purchases only among each completed path's forty highest real-GP means. Real feedback updates the complete archive and top-sixty-four breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add mean-supported intermediate sources during the existing stall regime: before each wave, form the sampled-value beam within the current path's forty highest cached real-GP means. This redirects bounded construction effort toward sources supported by the fitted mean while retaining coherent sampled preference, all admitted graphs, and the successful final purchase screen. The frozen sibling list is empty. The preceding improvement screened completed paths; this intervention changes which visited graphs can generate extensions. Losing useful low-mean intermediate routes is the explicit contrary prediction.

observed_bottleneck: On actual code Parent n-dc60d82e4f36, final eligibility is confirmed/not_triggered and must be preserved: 487/940 stalled purchases changed; complete equal-session positive scored-root gain rose from n-eb15da16dbea's 0.0030352346989319977 to 0.0035516224072537706, with endpoint mean 0.5780299607734479 and actual-Parent delta +0.013244312114626325. The limiting behavior is earlier in construction: CoherentGraphSearch.expand chooses its four sources entirely by sampled value, before the final screen runs. Re-reading and hashing all fifteen original Parent session logs reproduces the frozen census: 10894/30080 stalled beam memberships lie outside the pre-wave top40 real means, 4836/7520 stalled beams contain one, and 23585/64741 actual attempted extensions start from such sources. These are wrapper-call exposures, not counts of primitive subattempts or evidence of unbought rewards. Of all 4350 purchases, 3804 have zero positive root gain and mean sampled optimism is 0.14096400677019458. Final screening cannot restore branches not constructed. The source restriction might instead remove useful valley crossings, so final-screen success is only condition-bound precedent. Parent summaries, run logs, analyses and the reproducible fifteen-cell census are indexed in policy/scratch/r0077-01-improve-L01/plan/evidence-review.json and parent-evidence.json; every session audit cites its original log and trajectory. Formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de remains a distinct comparator at 0.607030316211131.

adoptions.applicability: The final mean screen cannot restore branches discarded by a sampled-value-only intermediate beam. The same observed stalled states devote substantial bounded expansion effort to sources the proposed pre-wave mean support excludes. Whether screening this source consumer sacrifices useful valley crossings is an open contrary prediction; final-screen success is not proof of transfer to generation.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Exact finite Gaussian function conditioning and persistent path identity.

deviations.adopted_setting: Retain the measured exact sampler; add only the internal-evidence source eligibility screen before bounded expansion.
deviations.paper_setting: Wilson studies posterior function sampling, not a mean-eligible molecular search frontier.
deviations.reason: Final screening succeeded, but23585/64741 stalled attempted extensions still originate outside the same pre-wave mean support.

adoptions.implementation_change: Add a pre-wave source-eligibility restriction to the inherited coherent path search, only when the existing real stall state activates K=3. Before each of the eight expansion waves, rank all identities already visited by that path by descending fixed real-GP mean with canonical ties, keep min(40,current_support), then form the existing four-member beam by cached sampled value within that set. Keep uniform selection within that beam, eight new graphs and 96 raw-attempt cap per wave, all primitives, exact coherent conditional values and identity cache. Newly admitted lower-mean graphs remain cached and may enter later top40 support; they are not structurally rejected. Preserve the independently measured final top40 screen, original nonstalled beam law and all paid allocation rules. This changes generation sources, not a beam-width, depth, gate threshold or acquisition-amplitude number.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse only the frozen position-two Wilson adoption and its exact applicability/deviation record from policy/scratch/round77-search-policy/literature-adoptions.json. The recorded discovery queries remain in the cited planning review; this PLAN made no new search query and opened the cited primary paper to verify its Gaussian-conditioning construction. Retain the already implemented exact finite coherent sampler. The new mean-supported intermediate source consumer is an explicit internal-evidence adaptation; neither the paper nor the Parent final-screen result proves its benefit. No feature approximation, model, dependency or checkpoint is introduced.

sources.applicability: Preserve exact measured finite paths and their identity cache. An intermediate source-eligibility screen is an internal adaptation, not a theorem in the paper. Conditional candidate integration uses Gaussian algebra without importing a new approximate prior or feature map.
sources.finding: Function-space Gaussian conditioning supplies coherent sampled values and conditional Gaussian distributions; scalable approximations are a separate construction.
sources.title: Efficiently Sampling Functions from Gaussian Process Posteriors (ICML 2020)

hypothesis: Modify only the stalled pre-wave source consumer of the existing coherent posterior-path graph search on n-dc60d82e4f36. At the start of each of its eight waves, let V be the canonical identities already visited by this path, with each identity reading its unchanged cached real-GP mean mu and cached latent path value f. When the inherited real stall state requests K=3/M=40 restriction, set E to the first min(40,|V|) identities sorted by (-mu, canonical identity), then set B to the first min(4,|E|) identities sorted by (-f, canonical identity) within E. Freeze B within this wave and keep the existing uniform source-index draw. Otherwise use the original unrestricted sampled-value beam exactly. Retain all successful admissions in V and the coherent identity/feature cache regardless of mean; a newly admitted lower-mean graph can be used at a later wave if its then-current mean rank qualifies. No graph is structurally rejected by this source rule. All eight-new-graph/96-raw-attempt wave bounds and independently applied final top40 eligibility remain. The hypothesis is that changing exposed construction sources redirects actual generated and purchased ancestry and strictly increases complete equal-session positive scored-root gain, rather than merely reducing sampled optimism.

finding_summary.headline: Source screening changed paid ancestry but reduced useful root gain across the full panel
finding_summary.insights:
The changed construction paths reached real learning and breeding: 332 of the 350 affected purchases entered a later fit, 306 survived their birth batch, 220 were later drawn as breeders and 127 had later accepted descendants. Yet 292 of those 350 did not beat their generating roots. The useful-transfer success of the retained final purchase screen therefore did not transfer to this intermediate source restriction. The Parent had 61 paid paths through sources outside the proposed stalled top40 support, including 14 that beat their roots. These observed useful routes make loss of intermediate options plausible, without identifying Child counterfactual outcomes or explaining the total loss. Lower-mean intermediates were still admitted and used.

The method still has difficulty turning locally attractive sampled paths into useful purchases: 3,816 of 4,350 purchases did not beat their roots. Mean sampled optimism fell from 0.140964 to 0.136756, while sampled-value ordering agreed with realized scores in 44.64% of nontied paid pairs within each batch, compared with 69.10% for the real-GP mean. This identifies a limitation on the selected stream; it does not establish universal GP miscalibration. Molecular evidence shows broad overall exploration but repeated local substitutions around some upper-score cores. Typed/generic scaffold coverage fell from 2,265/1,345 to 2,176/1,307, while reactive attachment chemistry, size extremes and unassigned configurations persisted. A proposal or search scheme that preserves alternative supported cores and intermediate routes, or a ranking model tested for actual descendant utility, could address these limitations; its benefit is unmeasured.

The borrowed exact finite Gaussian conditioning and persistent identity cache operated correctly. The source screen is the recorded internal adaptation, for which the literature supplies no benefit guarantee. This result refutes its registered full-panel useful-transfer prediction on this composition. It preserves the earlier final-screen confirmation and unguarded-path refutation, leaves mediation and retained-component contributions open, and does not end the broader approach.
finding_summary.results:
Correct source selection was verified in all fifteen Search sessions. Across 8,640 stalled waves, no actual source lay outside the permitted mean support. The restriction changed 35,362 of 73,469 source draws at the recorded drawn index and reached 350 of 4,350 paid purchases. All 4,200 nonterminal purchases entered the next real fit; the 150 final purchases had observed scores, with only later use censored.

Positive gain above real scored generating roots fell from 0.003552 to 0.003365 per purchase across the full panel, triggering the registered useful-transfer falsifier. Five task/seed cells improved, nine declined and one was identical; root-beating purchases fell from 546 to 534. Late gain improved from 0.001880 to 0.002049, but cannot replace the primary measure.

The endpoint mean rose slightly from 0.578030 to 0.578484, a paired gain of 0.000454, below the separate +0.002 development target. Seed macro deltas were −0.003147, −0.005792 and +0.010300. Paired task safety passes against the code Parent. Against the distinct formal Anchor, the mean is lower by 0.028547 and paired safety fails on sitagliptin_mpo. No technical failure or essential measurement gap explains the outcome.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring-rich output retains reactive heteroatom bonds, undefined stereochemistry and uneven control of size and ring topology
molecular.overall_character: The frozen comparison marks both Child evaluation and code-Parent pairing complete. All fifteen Child and fifteen published code-Parent trajectories were read; every trajectory has 300 accepted observations, including ten initial records and 290 optimizer products. No task or paired chemistry file is missing. Code Parent n-dc60d82e4f36 is distinct from formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de; there is no separate formal-Anchor chemistry comparison here. Across the 4,350 Child optimizer products, RDKit parses every molecule, finds rings in 4,289 and aromatic atoms in 4,261. The digest ring-marker rates are 0.9759–0.9966 and aromatic-marker rates 0.9713–0.9897; these are fractions of strings containing the markers, not fractions of aromatic atoms. The output combines fused and bridged systems, linked heteroarenes, partly saturated rings, amines, amides, ethers, imines, thiones and extensive halogen substitution. Both nodes have median size 31 heavy atoms. Child size spans 1–118 heavy atoms versus Parent 1–113, with 59 versus 61 products at six or fewer heavy atoms and 198 versus 217 at fifty or more. The chemical concerns persist despite graph validity: Child/Parent molecule counts are 1,248/999 for direct N–halogen bonds, 586/656 for O–halogen bonds and 344/287 for O–O single bonds. These flags overlap. Perceived rings of at most four atoms made entirely from aromatic atoms occur in 225/98 products; that is a geometry-review flag, not a proof that every flagged molecule is impossible. Explicit nonlegacy RDKit stereocentre perception gives 3,034/3,230 molecules with unassigned tetrahedral centres and zero with assigned configurations in either node. Formal-charge counts are also zero in both, which does not mean ionizable amines are absent. The Child has 2,176 nonempty typed and 1,307 generic Murcko scaffolds versus Parent 2,265 and 1,345; each has 61 empty scaffolds. Graph exploration is broad, while late and upper-score products often remain near a few session-specific cores. Fragment-excluded similarity is recorded separately for every seed, task and early/late stratum: Morgan radius 2, 2,048 bits, chirality enabled, nearest other molecule within that stratum, excluding products with at most six heavy atoms. No inferred target pharmacophore, synthetic route, conformer stability, pKa or biological activity is supplied by these scores. All reported functional-group counts are molecule-level graph queries defined in the audits; the neutral carbon-bound nonamide amine proxy is narrower than the historical Parent report, and uppercase-carbon amide matching does not enumerate every aromatic lactam. The original Parent report is preserved. Scores belong only to observed accepted molecules; no internally considered or passive alternative graph receives an inferred score. Chemistry associations do not decide mechanism activation, mediation, component contribution or a new performance criterion. Exact source/request hashes, extraction provenance and descriptor definitions are in policy/scratch/r0077-01-improve-L01/molecular/source-manifest.json, policy/scratch/r0077-01-improve-L01/molecular/log-extraction-provenance.json, policy/scratch/r0077-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and policy/scratch/r0077-01-improve-L01/molecular/stereo-method-refinement.json. The same-work-id request refresh is recorded in policy/scratch/r0077-01-improve-L01/molecular/request-refresh.json; only history/pending metadata changed, the original scientific audit hashes remain preserved, and validation uses the exact latest request. The Child raw trajectory copies are byte-identical to the frozen authorized staging sources; paid-feedback log extracts retain unmodified original lines and original-file hashes. All 290 paid log rows in each of the thirty sessions match their trajectory SMILES, scores and evaluation serials. Parent trajectories and logs are the published originals. The historical Parent report and descriptor convention remain at nodes/n-dc60d82e4f36/molecular.json and policy/scratch/r0076-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit_molecules.py. Per-task citations below include each paired trajectory, actual Child feedback-log extract, published Parent log and derived audit.

per_task.generated_character: Most products are moderately sized, heavily aromatic heterocycles: median 25 heavy atoms and three rings, range 1–48. Seed 0 peaks at a substituted benzocyclobutene carboxamide with vinyl ether, thioether and chloropyridylmethyl substituents; seed 1 peaks at a phenolic indole-like fused core linked through an enamine to a pyridine, with an N–O–Br termination; seed 2 peaks at a brominated ring nitrogen on a benzimidazole-like core bearing methoxy/vinyl ether, ethynyl and anilinomethyl groups. The three leaders have 25, 24 and 25 heavy atoms. There are 418 direct N–halogen, 71 O–halogen and 60 O–O products among 870 purchases, compared with Parent 58, 26 and 24. Ordinary uppercase-carbon amide matches fall from 548 to 280, while typed/generic scaffold counts fall from 354/135 to 265/98. Recognizable amide and heteroaromatic chemistry is present, but local attachments often make synthesis and stability questionable. liabilities: N–O–Br, N–F/N–Br and hydroperoxide substitutions occur in the observed high-score family; neutral valence-valid SMILES do not establish their stability.
The seed-0 leader includes an unsaturated four-member ring fused to benzene; local strain and a practical synthesis were not assessed.
Twenty-one purchases have at most six heavy atoms, including isolated atoms and small reactive fragments with zero or negligible scores.
missing_features: Lower-score and fragmentary products do not consistently retain the compact multiring heteroaromatic/polar-group arrangement associated with the observed upper scores.
Stable analogues spanning ordinary amide and ether attachment chemistry are less represented than in the code Parent; a reward for removing the unusual bonds is not established.
The trajectories do not identify an obligatory missing target substituent; the high-scoring examples themselves disagree about peroxide and N-halogen placement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader at evaluation 287 scores 0.47415709927863514; evaluation 297 swaps the phenol/N–O–Br pattern for hydroperoxide/N–F and receives exactly the same score. Thus the observed upper score tolerates chemically different reactive attachments. The seed-0 initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145, while its enlarged 48-heavy-atom peroxide-linked analogue at evaluation 23 scores 5.543355425209431e-18 and the tiny seed-1 peroxide at evaluation 230 scores zero. The ten highest observed Child products have 23–25 heavy atoms and aromatic multiring cores, whereas the ten lowest have 1–5 heavy atoms; neither indiscriminate enlargement nor fragmentation is supported by this gradient. The Parent seed-1 best is an ordinary N-methyl heteroaryl carboxamide at 0.5188745216627708, so the Child does not demonstrate a need to replace that chemistry with N-halogen motifs. Observed best scores in seed order 0/1/2 are Child 0.414503988226, 0.474157099279, 0.406486384378 versus code Parent 0.425402731076, 0.518874521663, 0.40735683193; the supplied signed deltas are -0.0108987428501, -0.0447174223841, -0.000870447552007. These are descriptive matched endpoints, not independent evidence for a chemical cause.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest output distribution: median 42 heavy atoms and six perceived rings, range 2–118. Many molecules combine several heteroarenes, imines, ethers, thioethers, carbonyl/thione groups and multiple halogens. The seed-0 leader has 44 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings connected by ether/imine linkages, plus an O–O–O chain and N-chloro substituents. Seed 1 has a 39-heavy-atom, six-ring bridged heteroaromatic product with small oxygen-containing rings, a cyclic carbonyl/sulfur linkage and N-bromo substitution. The size tail reaches 118 heavy atoms and the output includes dense fused/bridged systems; these features increase structural and synthetic complexity without proving a viable route.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
